title: Person Raising Hand Emoji 🙋 Meaning: “Me!” and “Hi!”
description: The person raising hand emoji 🙋 has one arm up like a student who knows the answer. It means “me!”, “I’ll do it,” “I have a question,” or a cheerful hello.
summary: 🙋 shows a smiling person with one hand raised high. It means “me!” or “I do,” used to volunteer, agree, claim something or ask a question, the way you would raise your hand in class. Many people also use it as a friendly wave hello or to get someone’s attention.
meaning: Think of a classroom. A teacher asks who wants to go first and one arm shoots up. That is 🙋: eager self-nomination. In group chats it answers questions like “who’s coming Friday?” or “anyone want the last ticket?” faster than typing “me.” It can also confess, as in “who forgot to lock the door? 🙋,” owning up with a grin.

The emoji’s original Unicode name was “Happy Person Raising One Hand,” and the happiness is part of the meaning. The figure is not asking permission nervously; it is keen. That enthusiasm makes it popular in audience-participation posts: “raise your hand if you’ve ever cried at a commercial 🙋” invites people to identify with a statement and reply in kind. Comment sections then fill with raised hands, a show of solidarity through shared habits.

A second use is the greeting. Because the raised arm looks like a wave, plenty of people open messages with “hi 🙋” or use it to announce their arrival in a chat. It also works as a polite interruption, the equivalent of “excuse me, quick question,” especially in work or class channels where someone wants to speak without derailing the conversation.

Many keyboards long drew the default as a woman, and the woman variant 🙋‍♀️ remains the most recognizable form. It carries a slightly bubbly, confident energy and appears in posts about women volunteering, single people announcing they are available, and anyone saying “that’s me, I’m the problem.” The man and gender-neutral versions are used the same way, with the neutral figure common in workplace tools.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It replaces “me!” in answers to open questions and offers. Friends use it to claim food, seats and plans, or to admit to a shared bad habit. As a greeting it is warm and a bit playful. One 🙋 after someone asks for help means you are volunteering, so be ready to follow through.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Creators use it for engagement prompts: “who else does this? 🙋‍♀️.” Followers respond with the same emoji in comments to say “guilty” or “same.” It also appears in introductions, such as “new here 🙋,” and in bios for people offering a service, where it means “that’s me, get in touch.”

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: This is one of the more useful workplace emojis. It signals “I’ll take that,” “I have a question,” or “count me in” without interrupting a thread. In video meetings, many platforms have a separate raise-hand button, and people type 🙋 in chat to do the same thing. It is polite, clear and rarely misread.

examples.meaning: Enthusiastically volunteering, with repetition for emphasis.

examples.text: 🙋 Quick question before we move on
examples.meaning: Politely asking for a turn to speak.
Looking for others in the same situation and counting herself in.

examples.text: Hi everyone, I’m the new intern 🙋‍♂️

examples.meaning: Offering to help or take on a task.

combos.meaning: Everybody is in; a whole group volunteering or agreeing.
A cheerful “that’s me!” or bright hello.

confusedWith.difference: ✋ is just an open palm and usually means stop, wait or high five. 🙋 shows a whole person and means “me” or “I volunteer,” with a friendly rather than halting tone.

👋 is the standard hello and goodbye. 🙋 can greet too, but its core meaning is putting yourself forward: answering, volunteering or asking. A wave acknowledges someone, while a raised hand asks to be chosen.
💁 holds a hand out to the side at shoulder level and reads as sassy or helpful explanation. 🙋 lifts the arm straight up to claim attention or say “pick me.”

avoid: Do not send it in reply to a request for volunteers unless you really intend to do the task.
Avoid using it to interrupt serious or emotional conversations, where its cheerfulness can feel out of place.
design: The emoji shows a person from the chest up, smiling, with one arm stretched above the head and the palm open. Which arm is raised differs by platform, as does clothing color. There is a gender-neutral base with woman 🙋‍♀️ and man 🙋‍♂️ variants, and every version supports skin tones.

faqs.q: What does 🙋‍♀️ mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She is saying “me!”, “I’m in,” or “hi.” If you asked a question, she is volunteering or agreeing. If it starts a message, it is a friendly greeting. It is upbeat and open, but it is not a flirting emoji by itself.

faqs.q: What does 🙋‍♂️ mean from a guy?
faqs.a: He is raising his hand: answering “who wants to…?”, offering to help, or waving hello. In response to “who’s single?” style posts it obviously says more, but in general it simply means he is counting himself in.
It can mean hello, since the raised arm resembles a wave, and many people use it that way. It is less common for goodbye. If you want an unmistakable greeting or farewell, 👋 is the standard choice.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🙋 and ✋?
faqs.a: ✋ shows only a hand and often tells someone to stop or wait, or offers a high five. 🙋 shows a person eagerly raising their hand, so it means “I do,” “pick me,” or “I have a question.” The second is far friendlier.
